en: The Hymn to Śrī Kāmākṣī In the boundary of the city of Kāñcī, seated upon the seat of desire (Kāmapīṭha), she who is the non-objective consciousness of all causes sports there; her vine-like limbs are as tender as a cluster of saffron flowers, and she abounds in compassion. 1.

I take refuge in Him who dwells in Kāñcī, who holds in His hand the bow, arrow, goad, and whip, who is bowed by the weight of His firm breasts, and who is the root of the bliss of absolute liberation.

The sovereignty of the Moon-crested Lord, His state as the singular essence residing within the splendor of Prakṛti, and His status as the youthful moon upon the crest—these shine forth as the ultimate purport of the Vedas. || 3 ||

I dissolve in Your primordial Maya, which possesses the luster of young sprouts; O Moon-crested One, I take refuge at Your feet, which are the sanctuary of the girdle and the dispeller of the suffering of those who bow before You. || 4 ||

O you who desire that which obstructs desire, O Mistress of Desire, situated in the center of the seat of desire! O lotus-like one, yielder of desires, digit of desire, pinnacle of desire, O you whose very eyes are desire—be present! 5.

May Kāmakoṭī protect me—she who holds the stream of bliss for those who achieve victory in battle, who is a basket of soft virtues, the foremost grove of Kadamba trees, whose sequence of conduct is praised by sages, who has enchanted millions of cosmic eggs, and who is the young bride of Paramaśiva.

Victory, victory to you, O Mother of the Universe, O Auspicious One! Victory, victory to Kāmākṣī! Victory, victory to the Daughter of the Mountain! Victory, victory to the Beloved of Maheśa! Victory, victory to the bearer of the moonlight for the sky of consciousness! 7.
